comment:
One data-preservation issue remains at `69220f1d53d5`: the legacy-file detector can delete unrelated custom rules.

## A one-line custom rule can be mistaken for the legacy template

In [`is_pure_omarchy_fontconfig`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/69220f1d53d512780293ab7af636a625a9d59a71/bin/omarchy-font-set#L53-L71), the normalization deletes entire lines containing `<string>…</string>` unless they also contain `<string>monospace</string>`. That can remove a complete custom rule from the comparison, not just the old font name.

For example, append this synthetic rule on **one line** inside `fonts.conf`, after the existing multiline Omarchy monospace block:

```xml
<match target="pattern"><test name="family" qual="any"><string>serif</string></test><edit name="family" mode="prepend_first" binding="strong"><string>Alternate Serif</string></edit></match>
```

The real scripts produced this result in synthetic homes:

```text
legacy block + one-line serif rule
  -> comparison discards the entire serif line
  -> file incorrectly classified as Omarchy-only
  -> font set deletes fonts.conf; new drop-in lacks serif rule
```

The same detector in [`migrations/1790098827.sh`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/69220f1d53d512780293ab7af636a625a9d59a71/migrations/1790098827.sh#L7-L32) also loses that rule **when the drop-in already exists**: copying is skipped, then `fonts.conf` is removed. Without an existing drop-in, migration copies the whole file, so the rule survives there.

**Impact:** custom fontconfig rules can still be silently lost. The setter case is an incomplete repair of the existing overwrite bug; the migration adds an update-time loss under the narrower condition above.

**Suggested change:** make both detectors accept only the complete legacy template, allowing variation only in its font-name value. Preserve files containing additional rules instead of deleting arbitrary `<string>` lines during recognition. Add the mixed one-line-rule case to the existing preservation tests.

**Verified:** the legacy-only control is retired, while the equivalent mixed file with the custom match spread across multiple lines is preserved. The deletion therefore depends on formatting, not whether the file contains customization.
